title: F. Trulimero Trulicina
statement:
Trulicina gives you integers n, m, and k. It is guaranteed that k≥ 2 and n·m≡ 0 pmodk.

Output a n by m grid of integers such that each of the following criteria hold:

It can be shown that such a grid always exists. If there are multiple solutions, output any.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains three integers n, m, and k (2 ≤ n·m≤ 2·10^5, 2≤ k≤ n·m, n·m≡ 0 pmodk).

It is guaranteed that the sum of n·m over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, output n lines, each containing m integers that satisfy the criteria. If there are multiple solutions, output any.

Input:
```
32 2 23 4 65 5 25
```

Output:
```
1 2
2 1
1 6 1 6
2 5 2 5
3 4 3 4
17 2 12 25 14
3 1 6 19 11
8 20 23 24 4
9 10 5 13 21
22 7 15 18 16
```
